verdict: OK to lend in Alappuzha coir, but only to coir pith, geotextile and organised mat units with verified raw-material cover; avoid small yarn/fibre factories squeezed by Tamil Nadu husk and yarn prices.
title: Alappuzha coir products: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
Coir is a husk-processing trade: husk and yarn come in, fibre, pith, yarn and mats go out. **The unit is a conversion shop, not a brand — margin lives in the gap between husk/yarn cost and the price of pith, fibre or mats.** Kerala produces 60 percent of world white fibre supply [5], so Alappuzha sits on the raw-material side of the chain. Small factories here are already hit by rising prices of yarn and husk coming from Tamil Nadu [2]. So when a proposal lands, check where the husk and yarn are sourced and at what contracted price; if the answer is 'spot market, Tamil Nadu', ask for the last six months of purchase invoices before anything else.

## Where cash sits and what has changed
**Cash is trapped in working capital, not capex — husk and yarn must be paid for before mats and pith are sold.** The rating methodology for comparable weaving businesses flags fixed and working capital intensity as the reason funding needs run high [8], and raw material is the largest cost line in such businesses [9]. Local news is mixed: the state is running a six-month door-to-door coir sales drive to 9 Feb with a 50 percent discount and a 30 crore turnover target, plus 4.56 crore capital infusion for 443 coir cooperative societies and 41 crore of dues already disbursed [3]. That is support for demand and for cooperatives, not proof of private-unit profitability. **Treat the subsidy and discount push as a demand bridge, not as margin.**

## The growth opportunity to pursue now
**Pursue coir pith (cocopeat) and coir geotextile converters first.** A national seminar on coir geotextiles for infrastructure and environmental projects was held at Alappuzha in October 2026 [1], and the state has announced a special scheme for coco peat production [3]. These are the borrowers with a product story beyond commodity mats. Second, lend to organised mat and pith exporters with diversified buyers. **Avoid small yarn and fibre factories buying husk and yarn at spot prices from Tamil Nadu [2] — that is where the price squeeze is landing.** India-wide exports are down 13.6 percent Apr-to-date in USD [D], so any borrower whose sales ledger is export-heavy needs a buyer-concentration check; collect from customer the top-five buyer share and the currency of invoicing.

## How to grow safely
**Structure against the working-capital cycle, not against the building.** Size the limit to verified husk and yarn purchase plus one conversion cycle; collect from customer the actual cycle days, since no local figure is published. Take monthly stock and receivables statements, monthly GST returns, and a quarterly raw-material purchase register with source state named. Kerala GST collections are running 10.3 percent Apr-to-date against India's 6.1 percent [D], which supports local demand but does not fix a single unit's margin. **Covenant on raw-material cover and on buyer concentration; if the top buyer crosses a third of sales, ask for the contract and the payment history.**

## Early-warning signs
- **Husk and yarn purchase price rising month on month [2] (monthly) -> reprice the limit or ask for a higher margin; if the unit cannot pass it on, stop enhancement.**
- **Receivables beyond the verified cycle (monthly) -> ask for the ageing and the buyer's payment proof; if two invoices slip, freeze further drawing.**
- **Sales leaning on the state discount drive [3] (monthly, to 9 Feb) -> ask what replaces that volume after February; if there is no answer, treat the account as seasonal.**
- **Export share rising while India-wide exports fall 13.6 percent Apr-to-date [D] (quarterly) -> ask for buyer-wise shipment proof.**

Sources on this city are thin: the local items are a seminar notice [1], a raw-material price report [2] and a government sales drive [3]; peer and rating material is undated [4][5][6][7][8][9][10]. Lean on first principles and the data pack where local evidence runs out.
watch: Husk/yarn price up two months running -> reprice limit or demand higher margin
Any invoice past verified cycle -> freeze further drawing until paid
Turnover gap over 10 percent -> ask for explanation and revised limit
Top buyer above one-third of sales -> obtain contract and payment history
watch_note: Trigger levels are policy suggestions (analytical framing), not data.
news_why: Rising Tamil Nadu husk and yarn prices squeeze small Alappuzha coir factories' margins.
